newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rebound to close higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rebound to close higher.

text.p: French stocks rebounded on Monday in line with other European stock and bond markets which rose after EU leaders agreed on a stability pact to enforce budget disciple after European monetary union is introduced.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 19.16 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,222.57, recouping half of last week's 1.66 percent loss. The CAC-40 futures contract ended up 15.5 points at 2,222.

Traders said market sentiment was positive on Monday and got a further boost from an early advance in Wall Street stocks. But they said investors are feeling cautious ahead of the Bank of France's annual news conference on Tuesday, the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting and a Bundesbank council meeting this week.

* Michelin shares were among the biggest gainers, closing up 2.47 percent to recoup part of their 4.45 percent fall last week on market talk of a capital increase. Officials at the company were not available for comment on Monday.
* Eridania Beghin-Say shares closed 3.38 percent higher. Traders said the rise appears to be a technical rebound.

* Shares in textile firm DMC rose 6.02 percent to 114.40 francs after chairman Jacques Boubal told the weekly Journal des Finances he expected the group to break even within two years. Analysts said they remain wary on the stock, noting Monday's rise still leaves it near its year low of 107 francs and far from its year high of 284 francs set in April.
* Lagardere and Thomson-CSF remained weak on concerns about the privatisation of Thomson that was recently relaunched with plans to sell Thomson-CSF separately.
* Oil majors Elf-Aquitaine and Total both closed up 1.4 percent after announcing deals to buy Iraqi crude under a U.N. oil-for-food programme to ease the hardships on Iraqi civilians.
* Shares in film company Pathe, which owns 17 percent of BSkyB, rose 4.82 percent, tracking the British group's rise on plans to boost investment in digital decoders.
* French utility Lyonnaise des Eaux proposed to pay 330 francs per share to buy out minority shareholders of its Elyo unit.
